basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Cap. II.—Vers. 2.) Et consummavit Deus in die sexto opera sua quae fecit. Pro die sexto,'. Migne prints the chapter at the head of this block.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. II.—Vers. 2.) Et consummavit Deus in die sexto opera sua quae fecit. Pro die sexto, in Hebraeo habet diem septimum. Arctabimus igitur Judaeos, qui de otio sabbati gloriantur, quod jam tunc in principio sabbatum dissolutum sit, dum Deus operatur in sabbato, complens opera sua in eo, et benedicens ipsi diei: quia in illo universa compleverit.
